# 2 Samuel Chapter 8 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 175v–176r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_008_page_001.jpg, 2SA_008_page_002.jpg

---

**8:1** And-it-was after this, and-struck David the-Pelishtim and-subdued-them, and-took David the-bridle [meteg] of-the-cubit [ammah] from-[the]-hand of-[the]-Pelishtim.

**8:2** And-struck Moav, and-measured-them with-the-line [chevel], making-them-lie-down to-the-ground; and-he-measured two lines [to]-kill, and-one full line [to]-keep-alive. And-became Moav to-David as-servants, bearers of-tribute [minchah].

**8:3** And-struck David Hadad'ezer son of-Rechov, king of-Tsovah, when-he-went to-restore his-dominion [yado — literally "his hand"] at-the-River [Euphrates].

**8:4** And-captured David from-him a-thousand and-seven-hundred horsemen and-twenty thousand foot-soldiers. And-hamstrung [vay'aqer] David all the-chariot-[horses] and-left from-them a-hundred chariots.

**8:5** And-came Aram of-Dammeseq to-help Hadad'ezer king of-Tsovah, and-struck David of-Aram twenty-two thousand men.

**8:6** And-placed David garrisons [netsivim] in-Aram of-Dammeseq, and-became Aram to-David as-servants, bearers of-tribute. And-saved YHWH David in-all where he-went.

**8:7** And-took David the-shields [shiltey] of-gold that were upon [the]-servants of-Hadad'ezer and-brought-them to-Yerushalayim.

**8:8** And-from-Betach and-from-Berothai, cities of-Hadad'ezer, took the-king David bronze [nechoshet] exceedingly much.

**8:9** And-heard Toi king of-Chamat that David had-struck all [the]-army of-Hadad'ezer.

**8:10** And-sent Toi Yoram his-son to the-king David, to-ask-him [of]-peace and-to-bless-him, because he-fought with-Hadad'ezer and-struck-him — for a-man of-wars of-Toi was Hadad'ezer. And-in-his-hand were vessels of-silver and-vessels of-gold and-vessels of-bronze.

**8:11** Also these the-king David consecrated [hiqdish] to-YHWH, with the-silver and-the-gold that he-consecrated from-all the-nations that he-subdued:

**8:12** from-Aram and-from-Moav and-from-[the]-sons of-Ammon and-from-[the]-Pelishtim and-from-Amaleq, and-from-[the]-plunder of-Hadad'ezer son of-Rechov, king of-Tsovah.

**8:13** And-made David a-name when-he-returned from-striking Aram [or: Edom] in-[the]-Valley of-Salt, eighteen thousand.

**8:14** And-placed in-Edom garrisons; in-all Edom he-placed garrisons, and-became all Edom servants to-David. And-saved YHWH David in-all where he-went.

**8:15** And-reigned David over all Yisra'el, and-was David doing justice [mishpat] and-righteousness [tsedaqah] to-all his-people.

**8:16** And-Yo'av son of-Tseruyah [was] over the-army; and-Yehoshafat son of-Achilud [was] the-recorder [mazkir].

**8:17** And-Tsadoq son of-Achituv and-Achimelekh son of-Evyatar [were] priests; and-Serayah [was] the-scribe [sofer].

**8:18** And-Benayahu son of-Yehoyada and-the-Kereti and-the-Peleti; and-[the]-sons of-David were priests [kohanim].

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — meteg ha-ammah:** An extremely obscure phrase, literally "the bridle of the cubit/forearm." It may be a figurative expression meaning David took control ("the bridle") of the chief city ("the mother city"). The parallel in 1 Chr 18:1 reads "Gath and its towns."

**v.2 — chevel:** The measuring line is used to determine who lives and who dies. Two-thirds of the Moabite captives are executed; one-third spared. The brutality is reported without commentary.

**v.4 — vay'aqer:** David hamstrung the horses — cutting the tendons to disable them permanently. This was standard ancient practice to prevent chariot-horses from being reused by a future enemy.

**v.13 — Aram vs. Edom:** The MT reads "Aram" (אֲרָם), but the context (Valley of Salt, which is near Edom) and the parallel in 1 Chr 18:12 strongly suggest "Edom" (אֱדוֹם). The difference is a single letter (resh vs. daleth), easily confused in Hebrew script.

**v.18 — sons of David were kohanim:** The statement that David's sons were "priests" is startling since they are not Levites. The parallel in 1 Chr 18:17 reads "chief officials" (*rishonim*), likely a theological correction. The Leningrad Codex clearly reads *kohanim*.

*— EMET*
